summary: There is far too little data to judge any bot. In both the stocks and crypto races, no bot has a single closed trade (a buy that has been sold again), so the evidence is thin (the rule of thumb is at least 20 closed trades). There is no backtest (a replay over past prices) to lean on either. I am suggesting no rule changes yet.

The live race is too young to judge: every bot in both races has 0 closed trades (finished buy-and-sell rounds), well under the 20 needed for solid evidence. The only live movement is Buy and Hold, up 0.22% time-weighted return (the return that ignores the timing of deposits) in stocks and down 1.77% in crypto. The bots are all in cash, so they trail by 0.22% in stocks and lead by 1.77% in crypto. The backtest (replay over past prices) adds some evidence. On unseen test data no bot beat Buy and Hold in either race. Tyler in crypto and Ryan and Nathan in stocks look like the weakest. Treat these suggestions as tentative.

suggestions.change: Add a cooldown (a waiting period) after each sell before Tyler can buy the same coin again, and only buy breakouts when volume is clearly strong, so he makes far fewer trades.
suggestions.why: The backtest shows -82.61% on Instant over 642 trades and -41.33% on Markets over 1004 trades, which points to fees and slippage (the gap between expected and actual price) eating the returns. Fewer trades should cut that cost. Live data has no closed trades yet, so confidence is only medium.

suggestions.change: Buy only after RSI (a 0-100 gauge of how oversold a share is) is under 30 AND the price has stopped falling and ticked up, instead of buying straight into the drop.
suggestions.why: Ryan lost 14.63% in the test period over 101 trades and 23.32% in practice, which suggests he buys falls that keep falling. Waiting for a first sign of a bounce may cut losing trades. This rests on backtest evidence only.

suggestions.change: Give the trailing stop (a sell level that follows the price up) more room, and skip re-buying a ticker soon after being stopped out.
suggestions.why: Nathan is meant to hold for weeks, yet he made 136 trades in the test period and returned -8.48%. That looks like being shaken out and re-entering repeatedly, which costs fees each time. Backtest evidence only.

summary: Live evidence is far too thin to judge any bot: no racer has a single closed trade in either race, and the bots are all still sitting in cash.
